claim: Tonight, I'm officially terminating Biden's expensive and unnecessary methane regulations to save consumers and energy producers
read: At a Lubbock, Texas, campaign rally on October 27, President Trump said he was officially terminating Biden's expensive and unnecessary methane regulations to save consumers and energy producers. The Environmental Protection Agency's October 27 news release states that the president and EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin announced the agency's latest proposal to revise the 2024 oil and natural gas regulations under the Clean Air Act. The proposal would rescind the Super Emitter Program, create new categories for well sites, restore 95 percent efficient flaring as an option for associated gas, and make other technical changes. It is a proposed rule signed that day, subject to a public comment period of at least 45 days and publication in the Federal Register. The claim does not match the cited record. The interesting fact is the scale of the projected savings. The missing fact is that the action remains a proposal, not a completed termination.

sources.title: EPA — Proposes Major New Revisions to Burdensome, Unworkable Biden-era Oil and Natural Gas Regulations, October 27, 2026
EPA prepublication proposed rule preamble (signed October 27, 2026)

script: Evening Check. At a Texas campaign rally, the president said he was officially terminating Biden's expensive and unnecessary methane regulations to save consumers and energy producers. The Environmental Protection Agency's own release that day describes a proposal to revise the two thousand twenty-four oil and natural gas rules. The proposal would rescind the Super Emitter Program, create new categories for certain well sites, and restore ninety-five percent efficient flaring as an option for associated gas. It is a proposed rule, signed October twenty-seventh, that will go through public comment and Federal Register publication. The claim does not match the cited record. Verdict: contradicted.

claim: The Alaskans for Mary campaign has no involvement with either Sullivan campaign and did not recruit any candidates into the race
read: The Alaskans for Mary campaign stated that it has no involvement with either Sullivan campaign and did not recruit any candidates into the Alaska Senate race. The New York Times reported on October 28 that aides to Mary Peltola received instructions in summer 2025 to comb voter records for people named Dan Sullivan, that the effort (internally called the ballot composition project) involved campaign lawyers and Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee aides, and that text messages and documents show the team worked to recruit Dan J. Sullivan and other potential spoilers. Former campaign manager Elisa Rios told the Times that Peltola was not directly involved but was “definitely aware.” The claim does not match the cited record. The interesting fact is the scale of the internal coordination. The missing fact is the campaign’s continued denial against the reported texts and interviews.

sources.title: New York Times — Inside Democrats’ Secret Effort to Stack Alaska’s Ballot, October 28, 2026

script: Midday Check. The Alaskans for Mary campaign says it has no involvement with either Sullivan campaign and did not recruit any candidates into the race. The New York Times reported today that a staffer for Mary Peltola was instructed in the summer of twenty twenty-five to find as many people named Dan Sullivan in Alaska as possible. The effort, called the ballot composition project, involved campaign lawyers and senior aides from the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee. Text messages and documents reviewed by the Times show the team worked to recruit Dan J. Sullivan and other potential spoilers. Former campaign manager Elisa Rios said Peltola was not directly involved but was definitely aware. The claim does not match the cited record. Verdict: contradicted.

claim: DOJ has long followed a policy not to take investigative steps relating to a candidate this close to an election if delaying the action will not jeopardize a criminal investigation
read: A letter from 175 House Democrats led by Rep. Pramila Jayapal to Attorney General Todd Blanche and DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin cites Justice Manual section 9-85.500 for the claim that the Department has long followed a policy against taking investigative steps involving a candidate this close to an election when delay would not jeopardize the case. The cited section states that prosecutors and agents may never select the timing of any action, including investigative steps, for the purpose of affecting any election or giving an advantage or disadvantage to any candidate or party. It requires consultation with the Public Integrity Section when an action is likely to raise that issue or the perception of it. The section does not establish a time-based prohibition on investigative steps near an election. The claim does not match the cited record. The interesting fact is the citation itself. The missing fact is the actual text of the provision.

sources.title: Letter from 175 House Democrats to AG Blanche and Secretary Mullin, October 26, 2026
Justice Manual § 9-85.500 – Actions that May Have an Impact on an Election

script: Morning Check. A letter signed by one hundred seventy-five House Democrats cites the Justice Manual for the claim that the Department has long followed a policy not to take investigative steps relating to a candidate this close to an election if delaying the action will not jeopardize a criminal investigation. The section they cite, nine dash eighty-five point five hundred, says prosecutors and agents may never select the timing of any action, including investigative steps, for the purpose of affecting any election or giving an advantage or disadvantage to any candidate or party. It requires consultation when an action is likely to raise that issue. It does not set a calendar cutoff. The claim does not match the cited record. Verdict: contradicted.

claim: There's 500 million Arabs in the world. And yet they don't produce science. They don't win the Nobel Prize. They don't win the Fields Prize. They don't win the Wolf Prize. They don't produce literature.
read: At a Grand Rapids, Michigan, campaign event Monday, Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said there are 500 million Arabs in the world and yet they do not produce science, do not win the Nobel Prize, the Fields Prize, or the Wolf Prize, and do not produce literature. Official Nobel records show Egyptian chemist Ahmed Zewail received the 1999 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for femtosecond spectroscopy of chemical reactions; he was born in Damanhur, Egypt. Egyptian novelist Naguib Mahfouz received the 1988 Nobel Prize in Literature, the first for a writer with Arabic as his native tongue. Jordanian-born chemist Omar M. Yaghi shared the 2025 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for metal-organic frameworks. Zewail also received the 1993 Wolf Prize in Chemistry. The claim does not match the cited record. The interesting fact is the scale of the assertion. The missing fact is the documented prize winners.

sources.title: Nobel Prize — Chemistry 2025 press release (Omar M. Yaghi)

script: Evening Check. At a Michigan campaign event, the health secretary said there are five hundred million Arabs in the world and yet they do not produce science. They do not win the Nobel Prize. They do not win the Fields Prize. They do not win the Wolf Prize. They do not produce literature. Official Nobel records show Egyptian chemist Ahmed Zewail received the nineteen ninety-nine Nobel Prize in Chemistry. Egyptian novelist Naguib Mahfouz received the nineteen eighty-eight Nobel Prize in Literature. Jordanian-born chemist Omar Yaghi shared the twenty twenty-five Nobel Prize in Chemistry. Zewail also received the nineteen ninety-three Wolf Prize in Chemistry. The claim does not match the cited record. Verdict: contradicted.

claim: 15% of Americans believe between 1 and 5% of NCAA athletes are transgender; 14% believe between 6 and 25%.
read: A high-engagement post reports a YouGov survey in which 15 percent of American adults estimated that between 1 and 5 percent of NCAA athletes are transgender and 14 percent estimated between 6 and 25 percent. An NCAA spokesperson confirmed that the current number of student-athletes competing in women's sports who identify as transgender is effectively zero, consistent with the association's policy. In December 2024 NCAA President Charlie Baker told a Senate panel that fewer than 10 of more than 510,000 athletes were transgender. In February 2025 the Board of Governors restricted women's-team competition to athletes assigned female at birth. The estimates do not match the cited record. The interesting fact is the size of the overestimate. The missing fact is the official count and the current policy.

sources.title: The Bulwark — New poll on sports, masculinity, and transgender athletes
NCAA — Participation Policy for Transgender Student-Athletes (effective February 6, 2025)

script: Midday Check. A high-engagement post reports a new poll. Fifteen percent of Americans said they believe between one and five percent of NCAA athletes are transgender. Fourteen percent put the share between six and twenty-five percent. An NCAA spokesperson confirmed the current number competing in women's sports is effectively zero. In December two thousand twenty-four, NCAA President Charlie Baker told a Senate panel fewer than ten of more than five hundred ten thousand athletes were transgender. The following February the Board of Governors restricted women's-team competition to athletes assigned female at birth. The estimates do not match the cited record. Verdict: contradicted.
